record.source: Report of the committee on a plan for the temporary government of the western territory, 1 March 1784 (the Avalon Project, Yale Law School): states two degrees of latitude apart, divided by the meridians of the lowest point of the rapids of the Ohio and of the western cape of the mouth of the Great Kanhaway, the land east of that meridian one state; and the ten names (Statehood Campaigns outline, Appendix A)
record.note: North of the 45th parallel, with the land north of the 47th that the report joins to it. The meridians pass through Wikidata's points for the Falls of the Ohio National Wildlife Conservation Area (Q3064799) and Tu-Endie-Wei State Park at the Kanawha's mouth (Q14714352): the report gives no degrees. Drawn on the federal territory the Newberry dates from Virginia's cession, 1 March 1784; the Ordinance of 23 April 1784 kept the lines and dropped the names. Not yet reviewed by the owner.
